event: Huawei added to the Entity List
note: effective 16 May 2019; published 21 May (84 FR 22961); checked 2026-11-02

event: Foreign direct product rule extended to chips designed by Huawei (tightened again in August 2020)
Hong Kong loses the licence exceptions that treated it better than China (removed as a separate destination, so treated as China, on 23 December 2020)
note: suspension announced 30 Jun 2020 (85 FR 45998); the December rule ends Hong Kong's separate status; event reworded (it said the June step already treated Hong Kong as China); checked 2026-11-02

event: SMIC added to the Entity List (tools for 10nm and below presumptively denied)
note: announced 18 Dec 2020; published and effective 22 Dec; checked 2026-11-02

event: Advanced computing and chipmaking-tool rules for China (A100/H100 class chips, tools for 16/14nm logic and below)
note: BIS press release; also 18nm DRAM and 128-layer NAND tools; checked 2026-11-02

event: Netherlands and Japan agree to join US controls on chipmaking tools
note: agreement reported by Bloomberg; the terms were not published and each country issued its own rules later in 2023; checked 2026-11-02

event: China announces export licences for gallium and germanium (from 1 August 2023)
note: China's counter-measure; MOFCOM and GAC announcement No. 23 of 2023; checked 2026-11-02

event: Update closes the A800/H800 gap and widens tool controls
HBM and 24 kinds of chipmaking tools controlled; 140 Chinese entities listed
AI diffusion rule (country tiers for AI chips)
note: announced 13 Jan 2025; published 15 Jan; rescinded in May 2025; checked 2026-11-02

event: Nvidia H20 and AMD MI308 need a licence for China
note: Nvidia 8-K filed 15 Apr 2025 (told on 9 Apr); AMD disclosed MI308 the next day; checked 2026-11-02

event: Export licences for seven rare earths and magnets
note: China's counter-measure; samarium gadolinium terbium dysprosium lutetium scandium yttrium; checked 2026-11-02

event: AI diffusion rule rescinded; guidance that using Huawei Ascend chips anywhere may breach US controls
H20 licences granted in exchange for 15% of China revenue
note: reported 10 Aug 2025 and confirmed by Trump on 11 Aug; AMD MI308 on the same terms; checked 2026-11-02

event: Rare-earth controls widened to foreign products using Chinese rare earths
note: MOFCOM announcement No. 61 of 2025; suspended for a year after the 30 October Trump-Xi meeting; checked 2026-11-02

event: Nvidia H200 sales to China allowed with 25% to the US government
note: announced by Trump on 8 Dec 2025; checked 2026-11-02

event: BIS moves H200 and MI325X class chips (TPP under 21,000, DRAM bandwidth under 6,500 GB/s) from presumption of denial to case-by-case review for direct US exports to China and Macau; Blackwell still denied
note: 91 FR 1684; announced 13 Jan; effective 15 Jan 2026; a 25% tariff on the same chips from 14 Jan; checked 2026-11-08

event: Commerce guidance: the licence requirement for advanced AI chips applies to any firm headquartered or parented in China wherever it operates; Blackwell banned for China
